ALGER, 16/08/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Le mi: ALGIERS, 08/16/2026 (Algeria Tech) — The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications announces the accelerated deployment of the IPv6 protocol across the entire national territory. This technological transition aims to meet the growing demand for IP addresses and modernize Algeria's digital infrastructure.
Lancement officiel du déploiement d'IPv6: Official launch of IPv6 deployment in Algeria
Le ministère de la Poste et des Télécomm: The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications has launched a vast plan to generalize the use of the IPv6 protocol across Algerian telecommunications networks. According to initial estimates, this transition is expected to cover all 58 wilayas by the end of 2027, with a minimum coverage rate of 80% as early as 2026. The project is part of the 2030 digital plan, which aims to bring the IPv6 penetration rate to 95% among licensed operators and Internet Service Providers (ISPs). Pilot tests conducted since 2024 in the wilayas of Algiers, Oran, and Constantine demonstrated a 30% improvement in network latency and a 40% reduction in costs related to IP address management.
L'Agence nationale de réglementation des: The National Telecommunications Regulation Agency (ARPCE) has published a strict schedule for national operators, including Algérie Télécom, Mobilis SA, Djezzy, and Ooredoo Algérie. These operators will need to progressively migrate their infrastructures, with a first phase dedicated to major urban centers (wilaya capitals) before extending the service to daïras and rural communes. The ministry has also set up a 2-billion Algerian dinar support fund to assist operators in this transition.
La généralisation d'IPv6 représente une: The widespread adoption of IPv6 represents a major step forward for Algeria, which is facing a progressive saturation of IPv4 addresses. With a population of over 45 million inhabitants and a mobile penetration rate exceeding 120% in 2025, the country must urgently modernize its infrastructure to support the growth of digital services. IPv6 offers a virtually unlimited addressing capacity (2^128 addresses), enabling the development of the Internet of Things (IoT), smart cities, and local cloud services. According to ARPCE projections, this transition could generate a direct economic gain of 15 billion Algerian dinars by 2030, thanks to reduced network management costs and the emergence of new digital services.
Sur le plan technologique, IPv6 améliore: Technologically speaking, IPv6 significantly improves the security of Algerian networks by integrating native encryption mechanisms (IPsec) and reducing risks related to Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. For citizens, this transition will translate into better Quality of Service (QoS) in rural areas, where infrastructure is often limited. Local operators will also be able to offer innovative services, such as advanced 5G networks or smart home solutions, which require stable and secure IP addressing.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
L'Algérie compte actuellement 32 million: Algeria currently has 32 million fixed and mobile internet subscribers, with a penetration rate of 75% in 2026, according to the latest data from ARPCE. The telecommunications sector accounts for 3% of the national GDP, with annual investments exceeding 50 billion Algerian dinars, mainly driven by Algérie Télécom and private operators. The 2030 digital plan, launched in 2022, sets the objective of bringing 4G coverage to 98% of the territory and deploying an additional 5,000 km of fiber optics by 2027.
L'ARPCE joue un rôle central dans la rég: ARPCE plays a central role in regulating and supporting sector players, ensuring compliance with international standards and fairness among operators. Algérie Télécom, as the historical operator, has already begun modernizing its infrastructure with an investment of 30 billion dinars dedicated to the migration to IPv6 and the improvement of its datacenters. Private operators Mobilis SA, Djezzy, and Ooredoo Algérie are actively contributing to this project, with quantified commitments to reduce their carbon footprint and adopt green technologies.
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Mr. Brahim Bouteraa, emphasized the strategic importance of this transition during a press conference held on August 15, 2026. "The widespread adoption of IPv6 is a national priority that aligns with our vision of digital sovereignty. We will support every operator and every wilaya to ensure a smooth migration without service interruption," he stated. Algérie Télécom CEO Mr. Mohamed El Amri confirmed that his group has already trained over 500 engineers in new technologies and invested 5 billion dinars in IPv6-compatible equipment.
Le calendrier de migration prévoit une p: The migration schedule provides for an initial phase of testing and training until the end of 2026, followed by a massive rollout in 2027. Priority wilayas include Algiers, Oran, Constantine, Annaba, and Tlemcen, where infrastructures are under the heaviest demand. ARPCE will organize regional workshops in each daïra to raise awareness among local stakeholders, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public administrations.
D'ici 2028, l'Algérie vise à aligner ses: By 2028, Algeria aims to align its digital infrastructure with international standards, while already preparing for the arrival of 6G and quantum technologies. The ministry has also announced the creation of a national observatory to monitor network performance trends and identify potential bottlenecks. A dedicated digital platform will allow citizens to report connectivity issues and track the project's progress.
